audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'1.75%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.10%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha registrato un rialzo dell'1.20%, il VIX è sceso del 2.56%. L'oro si mantiene sopra i 4857 dollari l'oncia, in rialzo dell'1.51%. Il petrolio è sceso del 9.07% a 90.38 dollari.

Un alto funzionario della Fed avverte che una guerra con l'Iran potrebbe scatenare uno shock sui prezzi duraturo. L'economia globale è ancora sotto tensione.

I dati macro USA più recenti mostrano un CPI YoY al 3.3%, un Core CPI YoY al 2.7% e un tasso di disoccupazione al 4.3%. La prossima riunione della Fed è cruciale per le decisioni future sui tassi.

Mentre le borse mondiali osservano la consueta pausa festiva, i riflettori restano accesi sul comparto digitale che rimane attivo 24/7. Bitcoin quota 77,000 dollari con una variazione del -0.16%. Ethereum è salita del 3.12% a 2,405 dollari. Il Fear & Greed Index è a 26, in zona Fear.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, con particolare attenzione agli indici PMI e ai dati sull'inflazione. Un saluto da Price Alert, arrivederci alla prossima puntata. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 
Traditional markets are closed for the weekend. 
In their last close, Asia wrapped up mixed: Nikkei dropped 1.75% to 58,476, while Shanghai edged down 0.10% to 4051.43. 
This sets a cautious tone for European and US markets, had they been open.

Focusing on the previous close for Western markets: 
The S&P 500 rose 1.20% to 7126.06, with VIX at 17.48 and a decrease of 2.56%. 
The Dollar Index stood at 98.10, down 0.12%. 
Gold holds above $4857.60/oz, up 1.51%, while oil plummeted 9.07% to $90.38.

Geopolitically, a top Fed official warned an Iran war could spark a lasting price shock. 
Additionally, oil tumbled nearly 15% after Iran said the Strait of Hormuz is 'completely open'.

Since traditional markets are closed, we shift focus to digital assets, which trade 24/7. 
Bitcoin is at $77,000, down 0.16%. 
Ethereum is at $2,405, up 3.12%, and Solana at $88.46, up 0.35%. 
The Crypto Fear & Greed Index stands at 26, indicating fear.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin is up two point six nine percent, trading above seventy seven thousand dollars, with significant ETF inflows of six hundred sixty three point nine million dollars. Ethereum is up three point one two percent to two thousand four hundred five dollars, while Solana and BNB are up zero point three five percent to eighty eight point four six dollars and two point five eight percent to six hundred forty four point one dollars respectively. The Fear & Greed Index is at twenty six, classified as Fear.

Thanks for tuning in and we'll see you tomorrow. Have a great day and goodbye from Price Alert.

articles.title: Implementing the digital euro project
articles.snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) is working on a digital version of the euro, a project started back in 2020 that is coming closer to fruition as the enabling EU legislation progresses. The ECB has designed a digital equivalent of cash, aimed at complementing physical euros for day-to-day payments. Its approach may be compared and contrasted with the US Federal Reserve’s reluctance to introduce a digital dollar and with the People’s Bank of China’s definition of the digital yuan largely as a bank deposit. Has the ECB’s rationale for the digital euro evolved over time, from a response to tech…

articles.title: Winning in the Donbas: What Russia’s 2014–2015 Campaign Reveals About Modern War
articles.snippet: It is clear that the U.S.-Israeli decapitation, airpower-centric, and precision strike campaign are again not enough to bring about the two countries’ strategic goals. The United States still finds itself potentially having to commit land forces into its war with Iran, yet many unknowns lurk, including a fragile ceasefire and a U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. articles.title: A New Security Architecture for the Middle East
articles.snippet: The tense negotiations between the United States and Iran have exposed the limits of bilateral diplomacy. With the crisis fueled by overlapping, interconnected conflicts, the only viable path forward is a broader regional framework that addresses the Strait of Hormuz, nuclear proliferation, Palestinian statehood, and proxy warfare.

articles.title: Book launch: World War Trade: Conflict, Containment, and the Emergent World Trading Order
articles.snippet: Globalization is not dying. It is being rebuilt. When the United States and China weaponized trade in 2025, many feared the collapse of the global economy. Markets plunged, supply chains fractured, and policymakers spoke openly of economic warfare. But the collapse never came. In his new book, World War Trade, published by the Centre for Economic Policy Research, Richard Baldwin argues that the real story is not the conflict between superpowers but how the rest of the world responded. Through quiet restraint, strategic adaptation, and a wave of new trade agreements, countries representing the…

articles.title: World Bank and IMF See Economic Slowdown Across Central Asia and the Caucasus
articles.snippet: The World Bank and International Monetary Fund are predicting growth rates to slow in the coming years across Central Asia and the Caucasus. Azerbaijan is projected to be the lone state in the two regions to buck the trend and register moderate growth. The economic disruption created by the US-Israeli blitz on Iran is a wild-card factor affecting growth projections, according to the two banks’ most recent updates. The World Bank’s Economic Update for the Europe and Central Asia region also cites geopolitical tensions and trade fragmentation…

articles.title: Why Diesel Prices Surge Faster Than Gasoline in Every Energy Crisis
articles.snippet: When a geopolitical shock hits energy markets, the same pattern plays out: diesel prices spike fast, while gasoline lags behind. According to data from the Energy Information Administration, since the conflict in Iran began through to 4/6/26, the national average price of gasoline has risen by $1.11 per gallon. Meanwhile, diesel prices are up $1.75 per gallon. That divergence is important because diesel underpins freight and logistics, amplifying inflationary pressures across the broader economy. We saw this exact pattern after Russia’s invasion…
